sourceChecks.claim: MySQL overview confirms multithreaded SQL client/server with multiple clients and relational tables; lesson scope is the normal separate-server deployment.
InnoDB introduction confirms default engine, transactional commit/rollback/crash recovery, row locking, clustered organization and foreign keys; engine-specific scope is justified.

SQL modes confirms invalid input error versus coercion/warning; official CHECK documentation confirms TRUE or UNKNOWN accepted and FALSE rejected with enforcement configurable, supporting explicit NOT NULL and version/mode checks.

COMMIT documentation confirms default autocommit and explicit START TRANSACTION grouping; InnoDB parameters confirms default redo flush per commit and crash loss under delayed settings. External HTTP is outside the SQL transaction boundary.

Isolation documentation confirms first-read Repeatable Read snapshot and different current locking rules; locking-reads followup confirms lock-before-check/update protection and commit release; deadlock handling requires transaction reissue.

Index types confirms clustered row storage and primary-key columns repeated in secondary records, including wide-key overhead and two-step lookup. Workload-based query planning is consistent with those structures.

Replication overview confirms asynchronous default and source writes versus replica reads; replication-threads followup explicitly separates receiver relay-log persistence from applier execution, supporting stale-read and loss qualifications.

Point-in-time recovery and binary-log followup confirm restoring a full base then replaying later events selected by time/position; retained continuous logs bound recoverability. Replicating a valid delete cannot preserve earlier state automatically.

InnoDB introduction supports the relational/transactional benefits; previously checked isolation, indexes, replication and recovery documentation grounds the operational costs and requirement-led synthesis.
